subject: [Action Required] Latency regression detected on omega-prime v3.4 — validation and rollback window
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@bluevault.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: [Action Required] Latency regression detected on omega-prime v3.4 — validation and rollback window

Anna —

Quick heads-up: our edge monitoring flagged a persistent p95 latency increase for BlueVault traffic starting ~08:50 PDT this morning. We correlate the start time with the omega-prime v3.4 rollout (canary -> full traffic at ~08:30). Key observations so far: 

- p95 has risen from ~240ms (baseline) to ~740ms for API route /v1/generate (sample: spans across 6 regions)
- p99 tail spikes up to ~2.1s on a small subset (~0.6% of requests)
- Successful rate is nominal but there is a small uptick in transient 503s (~0.3% increase)
- Continuous batching metrics show longer queue times for this model variant; KV cache hit rates unchanged

I attached a short trace export (tau-trace-p95-20280605.csv) with request ids and timings. Preliminary analysis from runtime shows increased kernel stall time for the model's attention kernel when sequence length >1024 — consistent with a tight regression in the kernel selection path for v3.4.

Options I want to propose and ask your permission for: 
1) Joint RCA & mitigation (preferred): run targeted perf tests with BlueVault traffic pattern; keep v3.4 pinned for 2 hours while we gather evidence.
2) Provisional rollback to omega-prime v3.3 for a controlled 30–60 minute window to restore p95, then roll forward once regression is confirmed and patched.

If you are comfortable with a rollback, we can open a provisional window as soon as 11:30 PDT today for ~30 minutes (we'd perform the rollback, validate p95, then either keep v3.3 pinned or roll forward with a hotfix). Ben and Markus are cc'ed to approve the rollback authority and ensure it follows the rollback playbook.

Requesting: your preference (1 or 2), and whether BlueVault ops can commit to a Zoom at 11:20 PDT for coordination.

Thanks — we want to minimize disruption and avoid an SLA escalation.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability (Americas)
Redwood Inference
From: Anna Lopez <anna@bluevault.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueVault SRE <sre@bluevault.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Action Required] Latency regression detected on omega-prime v3.4 — validation and rollback window

Thanks Hannah — we see the same in our telemetry (p95 jump around 08:50). Our SRE ran a quick test against v3.4 and reproduced p95 increase on sequences >900 tokens; CPU utilization on our side is normal.

We prefer option 2 (provisional rollback) to prioritize customer-facing latency while you debug. We need to be sure the rollback is reversible and that any change is non-disruptive to user sessions. Please confirm: 
- Expected customer impact during rollback window (error rate increase? connection drops?)
- Exact steps you will run (we need to share safe rollback steps with our on-call)

We can do 11:30–12:00 PDT today. Zoom / handoff: Anna, Tom (SRE), Mira (Platform). Can you include a quick checklist in-line so our on-call can follow?

— Anna Lopez
Senior Product Ops
BlueVault Finance
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Anna Lopez <anna@bluevault.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Action Required] Latency regression detected on omega-prime v3.4 — validation and rollback window

Hannah / Anna —

I authorize a provisional rollback to omega-prime v3.3 for the 11:30–12:00 PDT window provided the following controls are in place: 

- Redwood SRE will execute the rollback steps in rollback-playbook-v2.pdf (attached) and validate p95 at 5min and 20min marks.
- BlueVault SRE will have on-call present on Zoom to monitor customer-facing metrics and abort if unexpected errors >0.5% or sustained 5xx increase.
- Post-rollback we will capture a short blameless RCA with telemetry (expected within 48 hours).

Hannah — please add Product (marissa_cole@redwood.com) and CS (monica_patel@redwood.com) to the post-mortem thread once we confirm outcome.

Approved. Keep notes in the incident runbook.

— Ben
Ben Carter
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

Confirmed — BlueVault accepts rollback during 11:30–12:00 PDT. Zoom join at 11:20 PDT: https://zoom.us/j/123456789 (pass: redwood)

BlueVault attendees: Anna Lopez (product ops), Tom Reed (SRE), Mira Patel (platform). Redwood attendees: Hannah Schmitt (SRE lead), Ben Carter (ops), Markus Klein (runtime eng).

Notes for on-call: please monitor p95 for /v1/generate (us-west region), error rates (4xx/5xx), and user session continuity. If error rate spikes >0.5% sustained for 5 minutes, abort and notify both teams immediately.

We will share a short confirmation message after the rollback completes.

— Anna
